summary: One of the best albums to ever come out of South Africa. Shane was in his bag when he made this one.
title: Yellow
content:
Shane’s debut album. “They say vision is a blessing that the blind man cheats”, is a line from the first track (Yellow) of the album and right there I knew I had to tap in into the whole album. I am personally glad that I experienced this album when I was still high school. Anyone who knew me personally and properly back in high school will tell you that I used to listen to this album a lot.

Shane Eagle should be proud of himself that he dropped this much heat as a rookie in the game. The production by ShooterKhumz in this project layered out the overall feeling of this project, you can almost instantly tell this album has some sort of personal level to it. I remember listening for the first time and I could tell Eagle is highly influenced by J. Cole in the way he approaches his raps in this album. He tackles different aspects of his life in the album such as his reflections and thoughts, his feelings, his faith and relationship with God and being vulnerable over the love he lost.

This album screams simplicity and easy bars is sometimes all you need in order to create a classic and this album here is for sure a South African classic. The only feature in this album is KLY on Need Me which is a classic on the South African streets. From start to Finish, you can really tell that Shane poured his heart out to try and make a masterpiece, and he did just that.

My top three favourite tracks in this one have to be:

Aliens x Convos with God, MIHI and Can You See.
verdict: Very Good Album and I would suggest that if you have not listened to it or you haven’t sat down and listened to it proper, go do so after this review.
